1. (Currently Amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a destination, the method comprising:
a. providing a finger palette including:
i. a ring portion that is securable to a finger; and
ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion being at least substantially smooth to allow a user to spread or blend cosmetic product on the surface portion;
b. securing the finger palette to a finger;
c. depositing a cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette by first removing the cosmetic product from the container using an applicator tool; and
d. transferring the cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette to a destination using a separate application instrument different from the applicator tool used to remove the cosmetic product from the container.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, further including the step of removing the cosmetic product from a container before depositing the cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette, wherein the cosmetic product is removed from the container using a first instrument and transferred from the surface portion to the destination using a second instrument different from the first instrument.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein:
a. a first quantity of the cosmetic product is deposited onto the surface portion; and
b. a second quantity of the cosmetic product is transferred from the surface portion to the destination using a separate application instrument, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity, wherein the separate application instrument is distinct from any instrument used to deposit the first quantity onto the surface portion.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein:
a. the surface portion extends outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter; and
b. the surface portion is free, from any first point on the outer perimeter to any second point on the outer perimeter, of features that could trap cosmetics and complicate cleaning of the surface portion.

6. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the surface portion is at least substantially without protrusions extending therefrom, and wherein the surface portion is configured to be scraped by an applicator tool in an uninterrupted motion from the outer perimeter toward the surface center.

7. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the surface portion is at least substantially planar, and wherein the planar surface portion is specifically configured to facilitate controlled transfer of a portion of deposited cosmetic product to a destination while retaining a remaining portion on the surface portion.

11. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the finger palette is secured to the finger by passing the finger through the ring portion, and wherein the ring portion is configured to be removably and replaceably secured to the finger.

12. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is a first cosmetic product; and
b. the method further includes the step of depositing a second cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12, wherein:
a. the first cosmetic product is deposited on a first segment of the surface portion; and
b. the second cosmetic product is deposited on a non-overlapping second segment of the surface portion.

14. (Original) The method of claim 12, further including the step of blending the first cosmetic product with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion to obtain a blended cosmetic product.

15. (Original) The method of claim 14, further including the step of transferring the blended cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette to the destination.

18. (Currently Amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a work surface, the method comprising:
a. providing a finger palette including:
i. a ring portion configured to be removably and replaceably securable to a finger; and
ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion extending outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter, wherein the surface portion is at least substantially smooth so as to allow a user to scrape an applicator past the surface center in an uninterrupted motion while spreading or blending cosmetic product over the entirety of the surface portion;
b. securing the finger palette to a finger by passing the finger through the ring portion;
c. dispensing cosmetic product from a cosmetics container using a first instrument and placing a first quantity of the dispensed cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette;
d. removing cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette using a second instrument different from the first instrument; and
e. applying a second quantity of the removed cosmetic product to a destination using the second instrument, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity, wherein the second instrument is specifically configured to selectively remove only a portion of the cosmetic product from the surface portion while leaving a remaining portion on the surface portion.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 18, wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is dispensed from the cosmetics container using a first instrument;
b. the cosmetic product is removed from the surface portion using a second instrument different from the first instrument; and
c. the method further includes the steps of:
i. dispensing a second cosmetic product from a second cosmetics container using a third instrument and placing a third quantity of the dispensed second cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette; and
ii. blending the first cosmetic product on the surface portion with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion to obtain a blended cosmetic product, wherein the cosmetic product applied to the destination is the blended cosmetic product, and wherein the blended cosmetic product is applied to the destination using the second instrument or a fourth instrument.
